raw_case_text:
A 65-years-old Swiss fisherman, known for hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and gout presents with fever, epigastric pain, myalgia, and jaundice lasting for one week. Initial laboratory exam reveals acute kidney injury, liver failure, elevated troponin I, and thrombocytopenia (Table 1). Because of frequent arrhythmia (ventricular extrasystole) and an elevated troponin I raising the suspicion of myocarditis, he is admitted during 48 hours to the intensive care unit (ICU) for monitoring. 
Because of the initial presentation and the patient's occupation, leptospirosis was immediately suspected and treated with antibiotics (ceftriaxone). Initially, renal function improved. Serologies for Leptospira icterohaemorrhagiae were positive, confirming the diagnosis.
Suddenly, 7 days after the beginning of his hospitalization, he presented multiple-organ failure (MOF) of liver, kidney, and lung required mechanical ventilation and high doses of norepinephrine. His APACHE II and SAPS II scores were 37 and 80, respectively, which means an expected 90% mortality (see Table 1 for others parameters). 
Plasma exchanges were started, followed by continuous renal replacement therapy with high-volume hemofiltration (HVHF) at 70 mL/kg/h. He received five sessions of plasma exchanges and was treated during 72 hours by HVHF, followed then by 10 days of standard hemodiafiltration before renal function recovered. 
His ICU stay was complicated by a penicillin-resistant enterococcus bacteremia requiring vancomycin treatment. Because of the large doses of amines, he developed dry necrosis of both extremities. He also required transient pacing for extreme bradycardia. Hemorrhagic bronchial secretions caused several respiratory arrests. Finally, he developed a severe CMV colitis requiring sigmoidectomy and ganciclovir.
He stayed in ICU for 45 days and was released from hospital after 70 days. He received care for skin necrosis of the feet and he had a brief hospitalization to restore bowel continuity.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 65-year-old man presented with a 1-week history of fever, epigastric pain, myalgias, and jaundice.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began 1 week prior to admission with fever, epigastric pain, generalized myalgias, and progressive jaundice. Initial hospital admission was complicated by frequent ventricular extrasystoles and elevated troponin I. Although renal function initially improved, he experienced sudden collapse on hospital day 7 with multiple organ failure involving the liver, kidneys, and lungs, requiring high-dose vasopressors and mechanical ventilation.
subjective.past_medical_history: Past medical history includes hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, and gout. Occupation and epidemiological exposure: Swiss fisherman with regular freshwater aquatic and environmental exposure. Baseline medications and drug allergies are unmentioned.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, epigastric pain, myalgias, and jaundice. Additional review of systems is unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Patient was febrile and visibly jaundiced. Cardiovascular: frequent ventricular extrasystoles noted on telemetry; later developed profound bradycardia requiring transient pacing. Respiratory: hemorrhagic bronchial secretions causing recurrent respiratory arrests while mechanically ventilated. Extremities: developed bilateral symmetrical dry necrosis of the lower extremities secondary to high-dose vasopressors.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory evaluation revealed acute kidney injury, acute liver failure, elevated troponin I, and thrombocytopenia. Decompensation severity scoring: APACHE II score of 37 and SAPS II score of 80 (predicting 90% mortality).
objective.advanced_workup: Pathology and endoscopy from emergency sigmoidectomy performed during ICU stay confirmed severe cytomegalovirus (CMV) colitis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Severe leptospirosis (Weil's disease) complicated by acute myocarditis with ventricular arrhythmia, late multiple organ failure (hepatic, renal, and pulmonary), secondary penicillin-resistant Enterococcus bacteremia, vasopressor-induced distal limb necrosis, and CMV colitis. Confirmed by positive serologies for Leptospira icterohaemorrhagiae. Treatment & Outcome: Initially treated with intravenous ceftriaxone. Day 7 multiorgan collapse was managed with mechanical ventilation, high-dose norepinephrine, transient cardiac pacing, 5 sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange, 72 hours of high-volume hemofiltration (HVHF at 70 mL/kg/h), and 10 days of continuous hemodiafiltration until renal recovery. Nosocomial Enterococcus bacteremia was treated with vancomycin, and CMV colitis was managed with ganciclovir and emergency sigmoidectomy. The patient was discharged after 45 days in the ICU and 70 days total hospitalization, later undergoing elective restoration of bowel continuity and wound care for distal extremity necrosis.
